• Conflict resolution and mediation
• HRIS systems (SAP HR, BambooHR)
• Communication, empathy, and confidentiality
career.CareerProfile.title: Human Resource Manager

career.CareerProfile.description: Interior designers create functional and aesthetically pleasing interior spaces for homes, offices, hotels, and commercial buildings. Kenya's construction boom is creating strong demand for interior design professionals.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Consult with clients to understand space needs and preferences
• Develop space plans and design concepts
• Select furniture, materials, lighting, and colour schemes
• Prepare technical drawings and 3D visualisations
• Manage contractors and suppliers during fit-out
• Ensure designs comply with building codes and safety
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
• KCSE: C or above
• BSc Interior Design or Architecture (Interior Option)
• Diploma in Interior Design (TTIs)
• Portfolio of completed design projects
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: Rapid office construction, hotel expansion, and growing demand for quality home design among Kenya's expanding middle class.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities: Interior design firms, architecture companies, hotels, corporate offices, furniture companies, real estate developers, self-employment
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Creative visualisation and aesthetics
• CAD software (AutoCAD, SketchUp, Revit)
• Knowledge of materials and construction
• Client management and presentation skills
• Project management and budgeting
career.CareerProfile.title: Interior Designer

career.CareerProfile.description: Journalists investigate and report stories that inform and hold power to account — from TV anchors to investigative reporters, digital content creators, and podcast hosts.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Research, investigate, and verify news stories
• Conduct interviews and gather information from sources
• Write, edit, and present news articles or broadcasts
• Create multimedia content (video, podcast, social media)
• Build and maintain a network of contacts and sources
• Adhere to journalistic ethics and editorial standards
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Languages (English, Kiswahili) are key; minimum C+
2. BA Mass Communication / Journalism — 4 years (UoN, USIU, Daystar, Moi)
3. Or Diploma in Journalism (2–3 years at KIB, KIMC)
4. Internship at a media house (Nation, Standard, KBC, NTV, Citizen)
5. Build portfolio: articles, videos, podcast episodes
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: Digital journalism and content creation are transforming media. YouTubers, podcasters, and digital journalists can earn far more than traditional media salaries. Investigative journalism and data journalism are growing fields. Media personalities with strong social media presence are highly valued.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities:
• Nation Media Group, Standard Group, Royal Media Services
• KBC and county radio stations
• Digital media startups
• International media (BBC Africa, CNN, Al Jazeera Kenya)
• Corporate communications and PR departments
• Freelance digital content creation (YouTube, podcast, blogs)
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Strong writing and storytelling skills
• Research and investigative ability
• Broadcast presentation (for TV/radio)
• Video production and editing
• Social media and digital journalism skills
career.CareerProfile.title: Journalist & Media Personality

career.CareerProfile.description: Land surveyors measure and map the physical features of the earth, determining property boundaries and supporting urban planning, construction, and land administration in Kenya.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Survey and map land parcels, roads, and utilities
• Use GPS, total stations, and GIS software
• Prepare cadastral maps and land registration documents
• Provide topographic surveys for engineering projects
• Handle boundary disputes with legal survey evidence
• Conduct environmental and disaster risk mapping
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
• KCSE: C+ or above in Mathematics, Physics, Geography
• BSc Geomatics or Land Surveying — 4 years at UoN, JKUAT, Moi
• Registration with Institute of Surveyors of Kenya (ISK)
• Licensed under the Survey Act (Kenya)
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: Kenya's land digitisation program, urban expansion, and Big Four housing agenda create strong sustained demand for surveyors.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities: Ministry of Lands, National Land Commission, county governments, private surveying firms, construction companies, utility companies
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Mathematics and Geography
• GIS and remote sensing software (ArcGIS, QGIS)
• Precision and spatial reasoning
• Knowledge of land laws in Kenya
• Physical fitness for fieldwork
career.CareerProfile.title: Land Surveyor & Geomatics Engineer

career.CareerProfile.description: Animal husbandry specialists improve livestock productivity for meat, milk, eggs, and hides. With dairy and poultry being major sectors, this is a high-impact career for Kenya's food security.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Advise farmers on livestock breeds, feeding, and management
• Implement animal health and vaccination programs
• Manage breeding programs to improve stock quality
• Conduct farm assessments and productivity analysis
• Train farmers on modern animal husbandry practices
• Support value addition in dairy, poultry, and beef production
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
• KCSE: C or above in Biology
• Diploma in Animal Production (TVET — 2–3 years)
• BSc Animal Science or Range Management — 4 years at Egerton, UoN, KAU
• Optional: MSc Animal Breeding and Genetics
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: Rising demand for protein and dairy products plus climate-resilient livestock programs make this sector essential to Kenya's food security agenda.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities: Ministry of Agriculture, county government extension services, dairy companies (KCC, Brookside), large ranches, NGOs, Kenya Meat Commission
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Animal science and husbandry knowledge
• Practical skills in livestock management
• Communication and extension training skills
• Business skills for farm economics
• Veterinary first-aid knowledge
career.CareerProfile.title: Livestock & Animal Husbandry Specialist

career.CareerProfile.description: Marketing and sales professionals drive business growth by understanding customers, building brands, running campaigns, and converting prospects into loyal buyers.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Develop and execute marketing campaigns (digital and traditional)
• Conduct market research and competitive analysis
• Manage social media accounts and content calendars
• Build and manage sales pipelines and client relationships
• Analyse campaign performance using data and KPIs
• Collaborate with product teams and creative agencies
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Minimum C+; Languages and Business subjects useful
2. BA / BSc Marketing or BCom Marketing — 4 years
3. CIM (Chartered Institute of Marketing) professional qualifications
4. Google Digital Marketing certifications (free online)
5. Build a portfolio: managed campaigns, social media accounts, case studies
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: Digital marketing is disrupting traditional advertising. Data-driven marketing professionals with skills in performance marketing and CRM analytics earn premium salaries. Entrepreneurial marketers can build successful consultancy businesses.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities:
• Consumer goods companies (Unilever, Procter & Gamble, Bidco)
• Banks and financial services
• Media and advertising agencies
• Tech startups and e-commerce platforms
• NGOs for fundraising and communications roles
• Freelance digital marketing consultancy
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Digital marketing: SEO, Google Ads, Meta Ads, email marketing
• Sales techniques and negotiation
• Analytical tools: Google Analytics, CRM systems
• Content creation and copywriting
• Communication and public presentation
career.CareerProfile.title: Marketing & Sales Professional

career.CareerProfile.description: Mechanical engineers design, build, and maintain machines, engines, and mechanical systems — from industrial equipment and vehicles to HVAC systems and manufacturing lines.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Design mechanical components and systems using CAD software
• Analyse structural and thermal performance of machines
• Oversee manufacturing processes and quality control
• Maintain and troubleshoot industrial machinery
• Manage maintenance schedules and teams
• Ensure compliance with engineering and safety standards
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Mathematics and Physics are essential
2. BSc Mechanical Engineering — 5 years (JKUAT, TU-K, UoN, Dedan Kimathi)
3. Graduate Engineer registration (Engineers Board of Kenya)
4. Specialisation: Automotive, Manufacturing, HVAC, Renewable Energy
5. Professional Engineer registration after 3 years practice
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: Kenya's manufacturing ambitions under Vision 2030, combined with growing automotive assembly and industrial expansion, will require more mechanical engineers. Renewable energy maintenance and energy efficiency consulting are fast-growing niches.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities:
• Manufacturing plants (Kenya Breweries, BAT, Bamburi Cement, Coca-Cola)
• Automotive industry (vehicle assembly, maintenance)
• Government parastatals (KENGEN, KPA)
• Construction industry (HVAC, plumbing systems)
• Oil and gas sector
• Engineering consulting firms
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Solid Works, AutoCAD, ANSYS for design and simulation
• Thermodynamics and fluid mechanics
• Manufacturing processes and materials science
• Project management
• Problem-solving and mechanical aptitude
career.CareerProfile.title: Mechanical Engineer

career.CareerProfile.description: Medical doctors diagnose and treat illnesses, prescribe medication, and guide patients through preventive care — one of the most respected and impactful careers in Kenya.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Examine patients and take detailed medical histories
• Diagnose diseases and order diagnostic tests
• Prescribe and administer treatments and medications
• Perform minor surgical procedures
• Refer complex cases to specialists
• Document patient records and maintain confidentiality
• Educate patients and communities on disease prevention
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Minimum B+ (mean grade); Biology, Chemistry essential
2. MBChB (Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery) — 6 years
   — University of Nairobi, Moi University, Egerton, KU, Mt Kenya University
3. 1-year internship (mandatory, government hospitals)
4. 2-year community service (mandatory)
5. Optional: Postgraduate specialisation (3–5 years) — Surgery, Paediatrics, etc.
6. Registration with Kenya Medical Practitioners Board (KMPDB)
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: Kenya faces a severe doctor shortage — 1 doctor per 10,000 people versus the WHO recommended 1 per 1,000. Universal Health Coverage (UHC) implementation is creating unprecedented demand. Specialist doctors in surgery, oncology, and cardiology are especially needed.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities:
• Government hospitals (KNH, Moi Teaching, county hospitals)
• Private hospitals (Aga Khan, Nairobi Hospital, MP Shah, Avenue)
• NGO health programmes (MSF, AMREF, Red Cross)
• International organisations (WHO, UNICEF)
• Private clinical practice
• Medical research institutions
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Deep knowledge of human anatomy, physiology, and pharmacology
• Clinical examination and diagnostic skills
• Empathy and excellent communication
• Decision-making under pressure
• Attention to detail and analytical thinking
career.CareerProfile.title: Medical Doctor (Physician)

career.CareerProfile.description: Medical laboratory scientists analyze blood, tissue, urine, and other samples to help doctors diagnose and monitor diseases. They are the backbone of modern clinical diagnosis in Kenya.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Collect and process biological samples
• Perform blood counts, cultures, urinalysis, and biochemistry tests
• Operate and maintain laboratory equipment
• Analyse results and report findings to clinicians
• Conduct HIV, TB, malaria, and COVID-19 diagnostic tests
• Maintain quality assurance and biosafety standards
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
• KCSE: C+ or above in Biology, Chemistry
• Diploma in Medical Laboratory Sciences (KMTC — 3 years) OR
• BSc Medical Laboratory Sciences — 4 years at UoN, JKUAT, Moi
• Registration with Kenya Medical Laboratory Technicians and Technologists Board
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: Post-pandemic investment in diagnostics infrastructure is driving demand. Molecular biology and genomics are opening new specialisations.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities: Government hospitals, private hospitals, reference laboratories (KEMRI), blood transfusion services, NGO clinics, research institutions
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Biology and Chemistry competence
• Precision and technical accuracy
• Ability to work under pressure
• Knowledge of laboratory safety protocols
• Good observation and analytical skills
career.CareerProfile.title: Medical Laboratory Technologist

career.CareerProfile.description: Mining and petroleum engineers plan and supervise the extraction of minerals, oil, and gas from the earth. With Turkana oil and Kenya's mineral wealth, this field is growing rapidly.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Design mines and drilling operations
• Supervise extraction of minerals and petroleum
• Ensure worker safety in mines and oil fields
• Assess mineral and oil reserves
• Manage environmental impacts of extraction
• Optimise production processes
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
• KCSE: B+ in Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry
• BSc Mining Engineering or Petroleum Geoscience — 4–5 years
• Registration with Engineers Board of Kenya (EBK)
• Optional: MSc in Petroleum Engineering
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: Kenya's Turkana oil fields and expanding mining sector (titanium, gold, soda ash) guarantee growing demand for mining and petroleum engineers.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities: Tullow Oil, Africa Oil Corp, Base Titanium, mining companies, Ministry of Petroleum, NEMA, geological surveys, engineering consultancies
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Geology, Physics, and Mathematics
• Structural analysis and mine design
• Health and safety management
• GIS and remote sensing tools
• Project management
career.CareerProfile.title: Mining & Petroleum Engineer

career.CareerProfile.description: Network engineers design, implement, and maintain the communication networks that connect people and organisations — from enterprise LAN networks to national fibre infrastructure.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Design and implement LAN, WAN, and wireless network infrastructure
• Configure routers, switches, firewalls, and access points
• Monitor network performance and troubleshoot connectivity issues
• Plan network capacity and upgrades
• Maintain documentation of network topology
• Support voice over IP (VoIP) and video conferencing systems
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Mathematics and Physics essential
2. BSc Telecommunications / Computer Science / IT (4 years)
3. Certifications: CCNA, CCNP, CompTIA Network+
4. Entry roles: Network Support Technician → Network Administrator → Network Engineer
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: Kenya's broadband expansion and the roll-out of 5G networks will require thousands of network engineers over the next decade. Cloud networking and SD-WAN skills are becoming increasingly critical as organisations move to hybrid cloud infrastructure.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities:
• Internet Service Providers (Safaricom, Telkom, Airtel, Faiba)
• Banks and financial institutions
• Government ICT departments
• Large corporations with multi-site networks
• ISPs and data centres
• Telecommunications consulting firms
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Networking protocols (TCP/IP, BGP, OSPF, VLANs)
• Cisco, Juniper, or Huawei hardware configuration
• Network security fundamentals
• Linux and Windows Server administration
• Problem-solving under pressure
career.CareerProfile.title: Network Engineer

career.CareerProfile.description: Nutritionists and dietitians advise individuals and communities on healthy eating, manage therapeutic diets for patients, and address Kenya's nutrition challenges including malnutrition, diabetes, and obesity.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Assess clients' nutritional status and dietary needs
• Design personalised meal plans and therapeutic diets
• Counsel patients with diabetes, hypertension, kidney disease
• Conduct community nutrition programs and school feeding initiatives
• Conduct food safety and quality checks
• Research on food systems and nutrition policy
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
• KCSE: C+ or above in Biology, Chemistry
• BSc Nutrition and Dietetics or Food Science — 4 years
• Internship in a hospital dietetics department
• Registration with Kenya Nutritionists and Dietitians Institute (KNDI)
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: Rising non-communicable diseases (NCDs) and malnutrition create strong demand. Corporate wellness programs are a growing market.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities: Public hospitals, private clinics, schools, food companies, NGOs, World Food Programme, UNICEF, research institutions, hotels
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Food science and biochemistry knowledge
• Counselling and communication skills
• Attention to detail in dietary analysis
• Cultural sensitivity (Kenyan food traditions)
• Research and data analysis
career.CareerProfile.title: Nutritionist & Dietitian

career.CareerProfile.description: Optometrists examine eyes, diagnose vision problems and eye diseases, prescribe corrective lenses, and provide primary eye care across Kenya.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Perform comprehensive eye examinations
• Diagnose conditions like myopia, glaucoma, cataracts, diabetic retinopathy
• Prescribe spectacles, contact lenses, and low-vision aids
• Provide pre- and post-operative care for eye surgeries
• Run community eye health screening programs
• Dispense and fit corrective eyewear
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
• KCSE: B or above in Biology, Physics, Chemistry
• Bachelor of Science in Optometry — 4–5 years at UoN or Masinde Muliro
• Internship (1 year)
• Registration with Kenya Vision Institute / Optical Board
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: Kenya has a major backlog of uncorrected vision impairment. Growing middle class and smartphone use are driving demand for eye care.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities: Private optical shops, hospitals, NGO eye health programs (e.g., Sightsavers, AMREF), school vision screening, research institutions
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Biology, Physics, and Chemistry knowledge
• Fine motor skills and precision
• Good communication and empathy
• Analytical thinking and diagnostic ability
• Business skills for private practice management
career.CareerProfile.title: Optometrist

career.CareerProfile.description: Pharmacists ensure safe medication use by dispensing prescriptions, counselling patients, and advising healthcare teams on drug therapy — a science-heavy, patient-facing role.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Dispense prescription medications accurately
• Counsel patients on correct dosage, side effects, and interactions
• Review prescriptions for errors or contraindications
• Manage pharmaceutical inventory and cold chain
• Collaborate with doctors on complex medication regimens
• Compound specialised medications as needed
• Ensure compliance with pharmaceutical regulations
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Minimum B (mean grade); Chemistry, Biology, Mathematics essential
2. Bachelor of Pharmacy (BPharm) — 5 years (UoN, MTRH, Strathmore SMPC)
3. 1-year internship in a registered pharmacy or hospital
4. Registration with Pharmacy and Poisons Board Kenya
5. Optional: Masters in Clinical Pharmacy or Pharmaceutical Sciences
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: The pharmaceutical sector in Kenya is growing with local manufacturing expanding and UHC driving increased medicine access. Community pharmacy ownership is highly lucrative for entrepreneurial pharmacists. Global demand, especially in the Gulf states, also offers excellent opportunities.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities:
• Hospital pharmacies (KNH, Aga Khan, private hospitals)
• Community pharmacies (Chain pharmacies: Goodlife, Haltons, Medivet)
• Pharmaceutical manufacturing companies
• KEMSA and drug regulatory authorities
• NGO health supply chain programmes
• Academic and research institutions
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Deep knowledge of pharmacology and therapeutics
• Attention to detail (medication errors can be fatal)
• Patient communication and counselling
• Chemistry knowledge
• Inventory management and business skills (for pharmacy owners)
career.CareerProfile.title: Pharmacist

career.CareerProfile.description: Physiotherapists help patients recover from injuries, surgeries, and chronic conditions through physical rehabilitation, exercise, and manual therapy.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Assess patients' physical condition and mobility
• Design and implement rehabilitation programs
• Use electrotherapy, ultrasound, and manual techniques
• Guide patients through therapeutic exercises
• Manage musculoskeletal, neurological, and respiratory conditions
• Work with athletes on injury prevention
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
• KCSE: B or above in Biology, Chemistry
• Bachelor of Science in Physiotherapy — 4 years at UoN, Moi, KMTC
• Internship (1 year)
• Registration with Kenya Physiotherapists and Occupational Therapists Board
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: Growing sports industry and ageing population drive demand. Telehealth physiotherapy is expanding rapidly post-COVID.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities: Hospitals, rehabilitation centres, sports clubs, private clinics, armed forces, corporate wellness programs, NGO health missions
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Anatomy and physiology knowledge
• Physical fitness and stamina
• Empathy and patience
• Analytical and problem-solving skills
• Communication and motivational ability
career.CareerProfile.title: Physiotherapist

career.CareerProfile.description: Public administrators manage government services, implement policy, and coordinate resources to deliver public goods — from county government to national ministries.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Implement government policies and regulations at local or national level
• Coordinate public service delivery and community programmes
• Manage government resources, budgets, and staff
• Liaise between communities and government departments
• Maintain public records and prepare administrative reports
• Handle public complaints and service requests
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Minimum C+ (mean grade)
2. BA Public Administration / Political Science — 4 years (UoN, KU, JKUAT, Moi)
3. Competitive entry to Kenya School of Government (KSG) training programmes
4. County Public Service Board (CPSB) appointment process
5. MA Public Administration or MPA for senior roles
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: Devolution continues to create roles at county level across Kenya. Public sector reform is driving demand for professionally trained administrators. Entry to the national government through the PSC remains competitive but highly secure.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities:
• Ministry offices and national government departments
• County governments (47 counties)
• Kenya School of Government (trainer/facilitator)
• Public Service Commission (PSC) appointments
• Kenya Defence Forces administrative roles
• International governance organisations
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Public policy analysis and implementation
• Leadership and management
• Understanding of Kenya's devolution framework
• Communication and stakeholder management
• Budget and resource management
career.CareerProfile.title: Public Administrator

career.CareerProfile.description: Public health officers protect communities from disease outbreaks, promote healthy lifestyles, and ensure environmental sanitation. They work at county and national government levels, NGOs, and international health organisations.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Conduct disease surveillance and outbreak investigations
• Inspect food premises, water sources, and sanitation facilities
• Implement immunisation programs
• Lead health education and promotion campaigns
• Collect and analyse public health data
• Coordinate emergency health responses
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
• KCSE: C+ or above in Biology, Chemistry
• Diploma in Public Health (KMTC — 3 years) OR
• BSc Public Health or Environmental Health — 4 years
• Optional: MPH (Master of Public Health)
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: COVID-19 permanently elevated global investment in public health systems. Kenya's UHC rollout will absorb thousands of public health officers.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities: County health departments, Ministry of Health, WHO, UNICEF, KEMRI, CDC, international NGOs, water and sanitation organisations
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Epidemiology and statistics
• Environmental health knowledge
• Leadership and community mobilisation
• Report writing and data analysis
• Knowledge of Kenya's health policies and laws
career.CareerProfile.title: Public Health Officer

career.CareerProfile.description: Quantity surveyors manage the costs and contracts of construction projects — from small buildings to major infrastructure. They ensure projects are delivered on budget and that contractors are paid fairly.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Prepare bills of quantities for construction projects
• Estimate and monitor project costs
• Manage procurement and contractor tendering
• Value completed work and certify payments
• Resolve contract disputes
• Advise on cost control and value engineering
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
• KCSE: C+ or above in Mathematics, Physics
• BSc Quantity Surveying or Construction Management — 4 years at UoN, TUK, MUST
• Membership with Institute of Quantity Surveyors of Kenya (IQSK)
• Optional: MSc Project Management
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: Kenya's infrastructure boom (roads, affordable housing, airports) is creating sustained high demand for quantity surveyors.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities: Construction companies, government (KeNHA, KBC), property developers, engineering consultancies, World Bank/AfDB-funded projects, private practice
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Mathematics and numeracy
• Knowledge of construction processes and materials
• Negotiation and contract law understanding
• Attention to detail
• Project management skills
career.CareerProfile.title: Quantity Surveyor

career.CareerProfile.description: Radiographers produce diagnostic images (X-rays, CT scans, MRIs, ultrasounds) that doctors use to diagnose and plan treatment for illness and injury.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Operate X-ray, CT, MRI, and ultrasound machines
• Position patients correctly for imaging procedures
• Maintain radiation safety standards
• Process and quality-check images
• Assist radiologists in interventional procedures
• Maintain equipment and quality assurance records
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
• KCSE: C+ or above in Biology, Physics, Chemistry
• Diploma in Medical Imaging Sciences (KMTC) OR
• BSc Medical Imaging Sciences — 4 years
• Registration with Kenya Medical Laboratory Technicians and Technologists Board
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: Expansion of county referral hospitals and cancer screening programs will significantly increase radiographer demand.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities: Government and private hospitals, diagnostic imaging centres, cancer centres, mobile imaging units, military health services
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Physics and Biology background
• Technical aptitude for imaging equipment
• Attention to detail and precision
• Good communication (working with anxious patients)
• Radiation safety knowledge
career.CareerProfile.title: Radiographer

career.CareerProfile.description: Real estate professionals value, manage, buy, sell, and develop property. Kenya's housing boom and rapid urbanisation are creating exceptional opportunities in this sector.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Value land and buildings using professional methodologies
• Manage rental properties for landlords and investors
• Facilitate property transactions and negotiations
• Advise on real estate investment opportunities
• Manage property development projects
• Conduct feasibility studies and market analysis
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
• KCSE: C+ or above in Mathematics
• BSc Real Estate or Land Economics — 4 years at UoN, JKUAT, KU
• Registration with Institute of Surveyors of Kenya (ISK)
• Optional: MSc Real Estate or MBA
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: Kenya needs 250,000 new homes per year. Government housing agenda and growing urban population ensure long-term demand for property professionals.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities: Property agencies, Knight Frank, HassConsult, real estate developers, banks (mortgage departments), county governments, NHC, private landlords
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Valuation methods and real estate economics
• Negotiation and sales skills
• Knowledge of land laws and property acts in Kenya
• Financial modelling and investment analysis
• Communication and relationship management
career.CareerProfile.title: Real Estate & Property Manager

career.CareerProfile.description: Nurses provide compassionate direct patient care, administer treatments, monitor health, and are the largest professional group in Kenya's health workforce.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Administer medications and monitor vital signs
• Provide wound care, IV therapy, and bedside care
• Collaborate with doctors on treatment plans
• Educate patients and families on health management
• Maintain accurate nursing records
• Support patients during surgeries and procedures
• Respond to medical emergencies on the ward
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Minimum C+ (mean grade); Biology and Chemistry are key
2. Option A: Kenya Registered Community Health Nursing (KRCHN) — 3 years at KMTC
3. Option B: BSc Nursing — 4 years (Moi, UoN, JKUAT, KU)
4. Option C: Kenya Enrolled Nurse (KEN) — 2 years at KMTC (entry with C-)
5. Registration with Nursing Council of Kenya (NCK)
6. Specialisation: ICU, Midwifery, Paediatric Nursing, Oncology
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: Kenya has a critical nursing shortage, and international demand is equally high. Thousands of Kenyan nurses work abroad (UK NHS, US hospitals) earning significantly higher salaries. Specialised nurses in ICU, theatre, and midwifery earn the most.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities:
• Government and county hospitals
• Private hospitals and nursing homes
• Community health programmes
• International health missions (MSF, Red Cross)
• Diaspora nursing in UK, USA, UAE, Canada (highly sought after)
• School and corporate occupational health
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Clinical nursing skills and patient assessment
• Compassion and emotional resilience
• Communication with patients and multidisciplinary teams
• Critical thinking in emergencies
• Infection control and patient safety protocols
career.CareerProfile.title: Registered Nurse

career.CareerProfile.description: Secondary school teachers shape the next generation by teaching KCSE subjects, mentoring students, and preparing them for higher education and life.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Prepare and deliver lessons aligned to the Kenya Curriculum (KICD)
• Evaluate student progress through assignments, tests, and exams
• Provide individualised support to struggling learners
• Prepare students for KCSE national examinations
• Maintain student records and communicate with parents
• Participate in school co-curricular activities and administration
• Continuously update subject knowledge and teaching methodology
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Minimum C+ (mean grade); Strong grades in chosen subjects
2. Bachelor of Education (BEd) — 4 years, choose 2 teaching subjects
   — KU, Moi, Egerton, UoN, TU-K, Maseno, many private universities
3. Teacher Service Commission (TSC) registration and certification
4. Optional: MEd for HOD, Deputy Principal, or Principal roles
5. International teaching options: UK, Middle East with international schools
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: CBC implementation is creating demand for retrained and newly-qualified teachers. International schools in Kenya pay significantly more than TSC scales. Diaspora teaching in the UK, Middle East, and East Asia is a growing trend for Kenyan teachers seeking higher income.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities:
• TSC-employed public secondary schools (47 counties)
• Private secondary schools and international schools
• National schools (Starehe, Alliance, Mang'u, Limuru)
• International schools in Nairobi (IB, IGCSE curriculum)
• Online tutoring platforms
• Teacher training colleges
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Deep subject knowledge in teaching specialisation
• Lesson planning and curriculum delivery
• Classroom management and student motivation
• Assessment and feedback skills
• Patience, empathy, and communication
career.CareerProfile.title: Secondary School Teacher

career.CareerProfile.description: Social workers support vulnerable individuals, families, and communities — from child protection and mental health support to humanitarian response and community development.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Assess the social, emotional, and economic needs of clients
• Connect families with government benefits and community resources
• Support children at risk of abuse, neglect, or exploitation
• Provide counselling and psychosocial support
• Manage case files and write detailed reports
• Work with probation services, schools, and healthcare
• Advocate for policy changes to protect vulnerable groups
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Minimum C+ (mean grade); Social studies helpful
2. BSW (Bachelor of Social Work) — 4 years (UoN, Kenyatta, KCA, Moi)
3. Or Diploma in Social Work (2–3 years)
4. Internship/placement in a social welfare organisation
5. MSW (Master of Social Work) for senior or specialised roles
6. Registration with Kenya Association of Social Workers
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: Kenya's social challenges — urbanisation, youth unemployment, gender-based violence, and refugee crises — create consistent demand for trained social workers. NGO and international development organisation roles offer competitive packages for experienced professionals.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities:
• Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development
• Children's homes and child protection services
• International NGOs (UNICEF, Save the Children, Plan International)
• Hospitals (medical social workers)
• Community-based organisations
• UNHCR refugee support programmes
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Empathy and active listening
• Case management and documentation
• Knowledge of Kenyan social protection laws and policies
• Cultural sensitivity
• Resilience and emotional regulation
career.CareerProfile.title: Social Worker

career.CareerProfile.description: Software developers design, build, and maintain the applications and systems that power our digital world — from mobile banking apps to hospital management systems.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Write, test, and debug code in languages such as Python, JavaScript, Java, or Kotlin
• Design software architecture and database schemas
• Collaborate with product managers and designers
• Review code written by peers and mentor junior developers
• Deploy and monitor applications in cloud environments (AWS, GCP, Azure)
• Maintain and improve existing systems to ensure reliability and performance
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Aim for B+ or above, especially in Mathematics and Sciences
2. Bachelor of Science in Computer Science / Software Engineering (4 years)
   — Available at UoN, KU, JKUAT, Strathmore, Maseno
3. Industry certifications: AWS, Google Cloud, Meta Developer
4. Build a portfolio of 3–5 real projects on GitHub
5. Internship or attachment during 3rd year
6. Entry-level roles: Junior Developer → Mid-level → Senior → Tech Lead
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: Kenya's tech sector is booming. Nairobi's Silicon Savannah is Africa's leading startup hub, and demand for software developers is growing 30% annually. Remote work has opened global opportunities with USD-denominated salaries. AI and cloud skills will be critical by 2030.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities:
• Fintech companies (M-Pesa, Equity Bank, KCB, Safaricom)
• Tech startups in Silicon Savannah (Nairobi)
• Global companies via remote work (Google, Microsoft, Amazon)
• Government agencies (eCitizen, NTSA, IEBC)
• NGOs and development organisations (USAID, UNICEF)
• Freelance & consultancy work
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Proficiency in at least one programming language (Python, JavaScript, Java)
• Problem-solving and logical thinking
• Version control with Git
• Knowledge of databases (SQL/NoSQL)
• Communication and teamwork skills
career.CareerProfile.title: Software Developer

career.CareerProfile.description: Special needs educators support learners with physical, intellectual, sensory, and learning disabilities, ensuring every Kenyan child gets quality education in line with the government's inclusive education policy.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Develop individual education plans (IEPs) for learners with disabilities
• Use specialised teaching approaches (sign language, Braille, AAC)
• Assess and identify learners with special needs
• Coordinate with therapists, parents, and school management
• Adapt curriculum and learning materials
• Advocate for inclusive school environments
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
• KCSE: C+ or above
• BEd Special Needs Education — 4 years at KU, UoN, Maseno
• Diploma in Special Needs Education (TTCs)
• TSC Registration
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: Kenya's ratification of the UN Convention on Rights of Persons with Disabilities and the Special Needs Education Policy will massively expand this sector.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities: Government special schools, inclusive primary and secondary schools, NGOs (CBM, Light for the World), rehabilitation centres
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Knowledge of disability categories and learning difficulties
• Sign language and Braille literacy
• Empathy, patience, and creativity
• Behaviour management techniques
• Collaboration with multi-disciplinary teams
career.CareerProfile.title: Special Needs & Inclusive Education Teacher

career.CareerProfile.description: Supply chain managers oversee the flow of goods from suppliers to customers — covering procurement, warehousing, transport, and distribution. Kenya's position as East Africa's trade hub makes this a high-demand field.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Source and evaluate suppliers and negotiate contracts
• Manage warehouse operations and inventory
• Coordinate transport and freight logistics
• Track shipments and manage customs clearance
• Optimise supply chain for cost and efficiency
• Manage relationships with freight forwarders and clearing agents
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
• KCSE: C+ or above
• BSc Procurement & Supply Chain or Logistics Management — 4 years
• CIPS (Chartered Institute of Procurement & Supply) certification
• Optional: MSc Logistics and Supply Chain Management
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: The SGR, LAPSSET corridor, and e-commerce growth are transforming Kenya's logistics sector and creating significant demand for supply chain professionals.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities: Multinational companies, FMCG firms (Unilever, Nestlé), retailers, SGR / Kenya Railways, Mombasa Port, logistics companies, NGOs
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Procurement and contract management
• ERP systems (SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics)
• Negotiation and vendor management
• Analytical and problem-solving skills
• Knowledge of trade laws, Incoterms, and customs
career.CareerProfile.title: Supply Chain & Logistics Manager

career.CareerProfile.description: Telecommunications engineers design and maintain the networks — mobile, fibre, satellite — that connect Kenyans. With 5G rollout and fibre expansion, this is one of the fastest-growing engineering fields.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Design and deploy mobile and fixed network infrastructure
• Manage and optimise network performance (4G, 5G, fibre)
• Troubleshoot network outages and degradation
• Plan spectrum allocation and frequency management
• Integrate new technologies (IoT, satellite broadband)
• Ensure network security and resilience
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
• KCSE: B+ in Mathematics, Physics
• BSc Telecommunication Engineering or Electronic Engineering — 4 years
• Registration with Engineers Board of Kenya (EBK)
• Certifications: CCNA, AWS, Huawei HCIA
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: Kenya's ambition to become Africa's Silicon Savannah requires massive telecoms infrastructure investment, guaranteeing high demand.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities: Safaricom, Airtel, Telkom Kenya, Liquid Telecom, Kenya Power, CA Kenya, government, fibre infrastructure companies, consulting firms
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Electronics and signal processing
• Network protocols (TCP/IP, GSM, LTE)
• RF engineering and antenna design
• Project management
• Problem-solving under operational pressure
career.CareerProfile.title: Telecommunications Engineer

career.CareerProfile.description: Tourism and hospitality managers run hotels, lodges, resorts, travel companies, and event venues. Kenya's world-class wildlife tourism makes this sector a major employer and foreign exchange earner.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Manage hotel or lodge operations (front office, F&B, housekeeping)
• Develop marketing strategies to attract tourists
• Ensure excellent guest experience and service quality
• Manage budgets, revenue, and cost control
• Train and supervise hospitality staff
• Develop tour packages and itineraries
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
• KCSE: C+ or above
• BSc Tourism Management or Hotel Management — 4 years at KU, Moi, UoN
• Diploma in Hospitality Management (TTIs)
• Practical internship in a star-rated hotel
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: Kenya targets 5 million tourists annually. Recovery post-COVID and new tourism circuits (northern Kenya, coast) are driving hotel expansion.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities: Sarova, Serena, Kempinski, Fairmont, Kenya Airways, travel agencies, safari companies, county tourism boards, MICE industry
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Customer service excellence
• Leadership and team management
• Knowledge of tourism products and Kenyan tourism circuits
• Financial management and budgeting
• Languages (French, Chinese, German — value-add)
career.CareerProfile.title: Tourism & Hospitality Manager

career.CareerProfile.description: Urban planners design cities, towns, and rural areas to be liveable, sustainable, and functional. As Kenya urbanises rapidly, planners are critical to managing growth in Nairobi and secondary cities.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Develop land use plans and zoning regulations
• Design physical development plans for cities and counties
• Assess environmental impact of development projects
• Coordinate infrastructure planning (roads, water, sewers)
• Engage communities in participatory planning
• Review and approve building development applications
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
• KCSE: C+ or above in Geography, Mathematics
• BSc Urban and Regional Planning — 4 years at UoN, JKUAT, Moi
• Registration with Kenya Institute of Planners (KIP)
• Optional: MSc Urban Planning or Environmental Planning
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: Nairobi's population will double by 2040. Kenya needs thousands of planners to manage urbanisation sustainably.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities: County governments, Ministry of Lands, Nairobi City County, NEMA, planning consultancies, World Bank, UN-Habitat
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Urban design and GIS/spatial planning tools
• Knowledge of planning laws (Physical & Land Use Planning Act)
• Analytical and research skills
• Community engagement and stakeholder management
• Project management
career.CareerProfile.title: Urban & Regional Planner

career.CareerProfile.description: Veterinarians diagnose and treat diseases in animals, safeguard food safety, and support Kenya's livestock economy. They work with pets, farm animals, and wildlife in settings ranging from rural farms to Nairobi National Park.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Examine, diagnose and treat sick or injured animals
• Administer vaccines and preventive medicine
• Perform surgical procedures on animals
• Advise farmers on animal health and husbandry
• Inspect meat and dairy products for food safety
• Conduct disease surveillance for zoonotic illnesses
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
• KCSE: B+ or above, strong in Biology and Chemistry
• Bachelor of Veterinary Medicine (BVM) — 5 years at UoN, Egerton, CAVS
• Registration with Kenya Veterinary Board
• Optional: MSc in Veterinary Epidemiology or Animal Science
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: Rising demand due to growth in dairy, poultry, and aquaculture sectors. Wildlife tourism and disease surveillance also drive need for vets.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities: Private practice, Ministry of Agriculture, Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS), food processing companies, NGOs, pharmaceutical companies, research institutions
career.CareerProfile.skills_required:
• Strong science foundation (Biology, Chemistry)
• Precision and attention to detail
• Physical stamina for farm and field work
• Communication skills for farmer advisory
• Empathy for animals
career.CareerProfile.title: Veterinarian

career.CareerProfile.description: Welders join metals to construct and repair structures, pipelines, machinery, and vehicles. As Kenya industrialises, skilled welders are critical across manufacturing, construction, and infrastructure sectors.
career.CareerProfile.duties:
• Weld metals using MIG, TIG, arc, and gas techniques
• Fabricate metal structures, frames, and equipment
• Read engineering drawings for fabrication specifications
• Inspect and test weld quality
• Repair machinery, pipelines, and structures
• Operate cutting, bending, and forming equipment
career.CareerProfile.educational_pathway:
• KCSE: D+ or above
• Certificate in Welding and Fabrication (TVET — 1–2 years)
• Craft or Diploma in Mechanical Engineering (Fabrication) (TVET)
• Trade Test certification with NITA
career.CareerProfile.future_outlook: SGR maintenance, pipeline infrastructure (LAPSSET), manufacturing growth, and industrial parks guarantee strong demand for welders and fabricators.
career.CareerProfile.job_opportunities: Manufacturing plants, shipyards, construction companies, pipeline companies, government engineering workshops, self-employment

The KUCCPS placement window is open for a limited time. Mistakes made during this period can lock you out of your preferred course for a full year. Here are the five most common errors and how to avoid them.

MISTAKE 1: CHOOSING COURSES WITHOUT CHECKING CLUSTER POINTS

Many students pick courses based on what they want to study, without verifying whether their cluster points actually meet the cutoff. Wanting to do Law is great -- but Law at UoN requires around 42 cluster points in Cluster 16. If your Cluster 16 score is 34, you will not be placed, no matter how much you want it.

Fix: Calculate your cluster points on CareerNext before opening the portal. Filter courses by your actual scores.

MISTAKE 2: LISTING ONLY HIGHLY COMPETITIVE COURSES

Putting Medicine, Law and Computer Science as your three choices without any fallback is a gamble. If you fall short of the cutoff for all three, you are left unplaced.

Fix: Use at least one safe choice -- a course you comfortably qualify for -- as your third option.

MISTAKE 3: IGNORING THE INSTITUTION DIFFERENCE

The same course at different universities can have dramatically different cutoff points. BSc Computer Science at JKUAT may have a lower cutoff than at UoN or Strathmore. If your score qualifies you for JKUAT but not UoN, listing only UoN means you miss out.

Fix: Search by course and compare cutoffs across multiple institutions.

MISTAKE 4: MISSING THE REVISION WINDOW

KUCCPS opens a revision window after initial placement results. Many students miss this window because they did not know it existed or missed the deadline.

Fix: Save the KUCCPS calendar dates on your phone. The revision window is typically 1-2 weeks long.

MISTAKE 5: CHOOSING BASED ON FAMILY PRESSURE, NOT FIT

Choosing a course because your parents want you to, without genuine interest or aptitude, is one of the most common causes of university dropout and career dissatisfaction in Kenya.

Fix: Take the CareerNext career quiz. It maps your interests and strengths to career clusters. Use the results as a starting point for an honest conversation with your family.

The placement process rewards students who are prepared. Use the tools available -- including this platform -- to make informed choices.

When most students think about healthcare careers, they think of Medicine (MBChB) -- a 6-year degree requiring an A-minus or better. But Kenya's healthcare system runs largely on Clinical Officers, trained at KMTC in a rigorous 3-year diploma programme.

WHAT IS A CLINICAL OFFICER?

A Clinical Officer (CO) is a mid-level healthcare provider licensed to diagnose illnesses, prescribe medication, perform minor procedures, and manage patients -- particularly in district hospitals, health centres and dispensaries.

In rural Kenya, the Clinical Officer is often the most senior medical professional available. COs staff over 70% of Kenya's public health facilities.

WHAT DO YOU STUDY?

The KMTC Clinical Medicine and Surgery programme covers:
Year 1: Anatomy, Physiology, Biochemistry, Medical Microbiology, Health Systems
Year 2: Internal Medicine, Surgery, Paediatrics, Gynaecology, Mental Health, Pharmacology
Year 3: Clinical rotations across all departments, Emergency Medicine, Community Health

HOW TO QUALIFY

Minimum requirements at KMTC:
- KCSE mean grade of C+
- C+ in Biology, Chemistry and English
- C in Mathematics (some campuses require C+)

CAREER PROGRESSION

After qualifying as a Clinical Officer, you can:
- Work in government facilities (salary Ksh 35,000-90,000+)
- Join a mission hospital or private clinic
- Specialise in Surgery, Anaesthesia, Ophthalmology, Psychiatry, or Paediatrics
- Pursue a Bachelor of Science in Clinical Medicine (upgrade degree, 2 years) at UoN or KU
- Work with international health organisations (MSF, WHO, UNHCR)

If you scored C+ in KCSE with strong Biology and Chemistry, Clinical Medicine at KMTC is a path worth serious consideration.

Use CareerNext to check whether your grades meet the KMTC Clinical Medicine requirements.

Financing higher education is one of the biggest challenges Kenyan students face. Fortunately, there are more options than most families realise.

HELB -- HIGHER EDUCATION LOANS BOARD

The most widely used funding source for Kenyan university students. HELB provides loans and bursaries to students at public universities.
- Loan amounts: Ksh 35,000-60,000 per year depending on financial need
- Repayment: Begins after graduation and employment
- Application: helb.co.ke after KUCCPS placement

HELB also offers bursaries (non-repayable) for students from very low-income households. Apply as early as possible -- bursary funds are limited.

GOVERNMENT SCHOLARSHIPS

The Kenya government occasionally offers full scholarships through specific programmes:
- Presidential Scholarship (high achievers, usually A grades)
- County Government Bursaries -- check with your county government office each year

EQUITY WINGS TO FLY

One of Kenya's most impactful scholarship programmes. Targets bright students from disadvantaged backgrounds. Graduates continue to benefit from alumni networks and mentorship.

MASTERCARD FOUNDATION SCHOLARS PROGRAM

Available at several Kenyan universities including University of Nairobi and Strathmore. Covers full tuition, accommodation, and a stipend. Targets academically strong students from low-income families. Applications usually open between January and March.

DAAD (GERMAN ACADEMIC EXCHANGE)

Germany offers generous scholarships for African students at German universities, taught in English. Strong in engineering, agriculture, and development studies.

KCDF -- KENYA COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT FOUNDATION

Offers bursaries to students in TVET and university. Focus on marginalised communities. Apply via kcdf.or.ke.

PRACTICAL ADVICE

- Apply for multiple scholarships simultaneously -- there is no rule against it
- Start gathering documents early: KCSE certificate, birth certificate, ID, fee structure
- Write honest, specific personal statements -- generic applications rarely succeed
- Check your county and constituency bursary fund every year -- many local bursaries go unclaimed

Keep an eye on the CareerNext calendar page for updated scholarship deadlines.

The Kenya Universities and Colleges Central Placement Service (KUCCPS) is the body responsible for placing KCSE graduates into universities, KMTCs, TVETs, and TTCs. Understanding how it works gives you a significant advantage.

STEP 1: KCSE RESULTS

Once KNEC releases KCSE results (usually in December/January), your index number and results are automatically shared with KUCCPS. You do not need to do anything at this stage.

STEP 2: OPEN THE STUDENT PORTAL

Go to students.kuccps.net and log in using:
- Your KCSE Index Number (e.g. 12345678001)
- Your KCSE Year of Examination
- Your date of birth

STEP 3: MAKE YOUR COURSE CHOICES

You are allowed to select up to:
- 3 degree programmes (public universities)
- 3 KMTC programmes
- 3 TVET/TTC programmes

List your choices in order of preference. KUCCPS will place you in the highest-ranked course you qualify for.

STEP 4: PAY THE APPLICATION FEE

A small application fee (currently Ksh 1,500) is charged via M-Pesa. You cannot submit without payment.

STEP 5: PLACEMENT RESULTS

KUCCPS publishes placement results in batches. If you are placed, you will see your institution and course in the portal. If not placed in your first choices, you may be placed in revision rounds.

STEP 6: REVISION WINDOW

KUCCPS opens a revision window after the first placement round. This is your chance to change choices if you were not placed or if you want to try for a different course. Use this window wisely -- research cutoff points carefully before revising.

STEP 7: REPORTING TO CAMPUS

Once placed, you receive a joining letter with your campus reporting date. Bring your original KCSE certificate, ID, and placement letter.

COMMON MISTAKES TO AVOID

- Choosing a course because of pressure from family without checking if you qualify
- Listing only highly competitive courses without any fallback choices
- Missing the revision window deadline
- Not verifying that your KCSE results in the portal are correct

Use CareerNext to simulate your placement -- calculate your cluster points, see which courses you qualify for, and plan your choices before the portal opens.

resources.Article.content:
One of the most important decisions after KCSE is choosing between university, TVET, KMTC or a TTC. Each path leads to a different destination. Neither is inferior -- they serve different goals.

UNIVERSITY DEGREES

Duration: 4-6 years
Entry: Minimum C+ for most programmes; A-B for competitive courses
Outcome: Bachelor's degree, eligible for professional registration in fields like Medicine, Law, Engineering

Best for students who:
- Scored C+ and above
- Want to enter professions that require degree-level qualification
- Are comfortable with a longer academic journey before employment
- Have a specific career in mind that is degree-gated (doctor, engineer, architect, lawyer)

TVET DIPLOMAS & CERTIFICATES

Duration: 1-3 years
Entry: D+ to C, depending on the programme
Outcome: Certificate or Diploma in a specific trade or technical skill

Best for students who:
- Scored below C+ in KCSE
- Want to enter the job market faster
- Are practically minded -- prefer building, making, fixing, or designing over classroom learning
- Want to start a business in a trade (welding, electrical, plumbing, fashion, ICT)

THE SALARY MYTH

Many families assume university graduates always earn more. This is increasingly not true. A qualified electrician or plumber running their own business often out-earns an Arts graduate on a starting salary. A TVET graduate with 3 years of experience can be more employable than a fresh degree holder in many sectors.

PROGRESSION ROUTES

TVET is not a dead end. Most colleges allow graduates to top up to a degree through bridging programmes. Diploma holders can join degree programmes at Part 2 in many universities, cutting the degree to 2-3 additional years.

THE HONEST QUESTION

Ask yourself: what problem do I want to spend my career solving? That answer -- not your KCSE grade -- should guide your choice.

Use CareerNext to explore both university and TVET courses side by side based on your actual cluster points.

resources.Article.content:
Kenya Medical Training College (KMTC) is one of the most sought-after institutions in Kenya. With campuses in every county and over 50 health training programmes, it is the primary route into clinical and community health careers for diploma-level students.

INTAKES

KMTC typically runs two intakes per year:
- January/February Intake -- applications open around October/November
- September Intake -- applications open around June/July

MINIMUM ENTRY REQUIREMENTS

For most KMTC programmes, the minimum entry requirement is a mean grade of C (plain) in KCSE, plus specific subject requirements depending on the programme.

Most competitive programmes (such as Clinical Medicine and Pharmacy) require C+ and above, with strong grades in Biology, Chemistry and English.

TOP PROGRAMMES AND TYPICAL REQUIREMENTS

- Clinical Medicine & Surgery -- C+ overall, C+ in Biology, Chemistry and English
- Pharmacy -- C+ overall, B in Chemistry, C+ in Biology and Maths
- Nursing -- C overall, C+ in Biology and English
- Medical Laboratory Sciences -- C+ overall, C+ in Biology and Chemistry
- Health Records & Information Management -- C overall, C in English and Maths
- Community Health -- C overall, C in Biology
- Nutrition & Dietetics -- C overall, C+ in Biology and Chemistry

APPLICATION PROCESS

1. Visit the KUCCPS student portal (students.kuccps.net)
2. Log in with your KCSE index number and year
3. Select KMTC under institution type
4. Choose up to three programmes in order of preference
5. Submit and wait for placement results

TIPS FOR BETTER PLACEMENT

- List your most competitive programme first -- KUCCPS places you in the highest-ranked course you qualify for
- Check cluster point cutoffs from previous intakes to gauge your chances
- Consider county campuses -- they often have slightly lower competition than Nairobi campuses

Use CareerNext to calculate your cluster points for health-related clusters and see which KMTC programmes you qualify for.

Many students assume that university is out of reach unless they scored an A or B+. That is not true. KUCCPS lists dozens of degree programmes with cluster point cutoffs well within reach of C+ and B- students.

EDUCATION DEGREES

Bachelor of Education programmes -- particularly in Arts, Science and Special Needs -- regularly have cluster cutoffs in the 30-38 range. If you are passionate about teaching, this is a realistic and rewarding path.

AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES

Courses like BSc Agriculture, Horticulture and Food Science at many public universities have cutoffs in the 34-42 range. Kenya's growing agri-sector makes these graduates highly employable.

ENVIRONMENTAL STUDIES

Environmental Science, Natural Resource Management, and Forestry programmes attract fewer applicants than Medicine or Law, keeping cutoffs lower while career prospects remain strong.

SOCIAL WORK & COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT

These programmes are vital for Kenya's development sector and NGO ecosystem. Cutoffs are typically in the 30-36 range.

LIBRARY & INFORMATION SCIENCE

An underrated but stable profession. Most universities offer this at cutoffs accessible to C+ students.

LINGUISTICS & LANGUAGE STUDIES

If you performed well in English or Kiswahili, Linguistics and Literature programmes could be your route into university.

RECORDS MANAGEMENT

A growing field as organisations digitise. Cutoffs remain competitive for students with a C+ aggregate.

PHYSICAL EDUCATION & SPORTS SCIENCE

If you are athletic and academically solid, this programme combines both and has accessible cluster point requirements.

HOW TO FIND YOUR SPECIFIC CUTOFFS

Use the CareerNext course finder to search by cluster points. Enter your grades, calculate your cluster points, and filter courses to see exactly which ones you qualify for.

resources.Article.author: CareerNext Editorial
resources.Article.content:
Every year, thousands of KCSE candidates miss out on their preferred courses not because of poor grades, but because they do not understand how cluster points work. This guide explains everything.

WHAT ARE CLUSTER POINTS?

Cluster points are scores (out of 48) used by KUCCPS to rank students for specific courses. Each course belongs to a cluster group, and each cluster uses a specific combination of subjects to compute your score.

The official formula is:

Cluster Points = 48 x sqrt((core subjects total / 48) x (aggregate total / 84))

This means two things matter equally: how well you performed in the specific subjects a course cares about, AND your overall KCSE aggregate.

THE 7-SUBJECT AGGREGATE

Your aggregate (out of 84) is calculated using exactly 7 subjects:
- Mathematics (compulsory)
- Best of English or Kiswahili
- Your next 5 best subjects

The maximum aggregate is 84 points (12 points per subject x 7 subjects).

WHAT ARE CLUSTERS?

KUCCPS groups all degree, diploma and certificate programmes into 20 calculation clusters. For example:
- Cluster 1 (Pure Sciences): Maths, Biology, Chemistry, Physics
- Cluster 5 (Engineering): Maths, Physics, Chemistry
- Cluster 14 (Social Sciences): English/Kiswahili, History, Geography, CRE/IRE

Your score in the cluster that a course belongs to determines whether you qualify.

MINIMUM CLUSTER POINTS

Each course at every institution has a minimum cluster point cutoff. If your cluster points for that cluster exceed the cutoff, you qualify. If not, you do not -- regardless of your mean grade.

This is why a student with a B plain (mean grade) might qualify for Medicine while another with a B+ does not, if the B student had stronger scores in Biology, Chemistry and Physics specifically.

HOW TO IMPROVE YOUR CHANCES

1. Know which cluster your target course uses before your exam
2. Focus revision energy on the specific 4 subjects in that cluster
3. Use CareerNext to simulate different grade combinations and see how your cluster points change

Use the free calculator on this site to compute your exact cluster points for all 20 clusters instantly.

CareerNext uses the KUCCPS weighted formula:

Cluster Points = 48 × √( (cluster_marks / 400) × (aggregate / 84) )

Where cluster_marks is the sum of the midpoint raw marks for your 4 cluster subjects (A = 90.2, B = 66, C = 50 and so on, out of 400), and aggregate is your KCSE total out of 84. The maximum possible cluster points score is 48.

The aggregate is your best 7 subjects scored as follows:

Mathematics + best of (English or Kiswahili) + your next 5 best subjects. The maximum aggregate is 84 points (7 subjects × A = 12 each).

resources.FAQItem.question: What is CareerNext?

CareerNext (this website) is an independent tool to help you prepare for that application — by calculating your points and finding your eligible courses before the portal opens. We are not affiliated with the government.
